sts3215.source: Feetech ST-3215-C018 datasheet (references/vendor/feetech-sts3215/ST-3215-C018.pdf): 30 kg cm, 45 rpm, backlash <= 0.5 deg, 0.088 deg/pulse; checked 2026-10-27

recoil.pan_moment: zero: the ball path lies in the pan axis's plane (y = 0) and both tyres push alike
recoil.on_the_robot: a 30-ball hopper dump is 0.9 N s: 0.05 m/s on a 17 kg robot (docs/head-payload.md budget 0.05 N s per shot)

gyroscopic.pan_note: the spin axes are parallel to the pan axis: no gyroscopic torque
gyroscopic.pair_note: the two tyres counter-rotate: equal and opposite on the cartridge, net zero; each Snail mount sees the per-wheel value

tilt.pulse_note: the pulse exceeds nothing the servo must hold continuously; it turns the tilting group 1-2 mrad against gravity's preload inside the gear lash (recoil.aim_shift_mrad)

pan.note: speed-limited, not torque-limited: 45 rpm through 3:1 is 90 deg/s at the turret, so the 90 deg in 1.2 s move (150 deg/s peak) is not reachable; recoil adds no pan moment

servo_margins.source: catalog feetech-sts3215-c018-12v (Waveshare ST3215: 30 kg.cm, 45 rpm at 12 V)

recoil_tilt_kick.note: stopped by the gravity preload inside the backlash

pan_gear_backlash_total.note: 0.15 mm per flank on the 63 T ring: the lash the pan can sit anywhere in when the load reverses

tilt_servo_backlash.note: direct drive: the full 0.5 deg; gravity preloads it nose-up, recoil pushes nose-down

pan_slew_30_deg_s.note: the muzzle's own sideways velocity (155 mm from the pan axis) adds to the ball's

pan_slew_90_deg_s.note: the muzzle's own sideways velocity (155 mm from the pan axis) adds to the ball's

pan_slew_150_deg_s.note: the muzzle's own sideways velocity (155 mm from the pan axis) adds to the ball's
